verdict: Easy to prototype, slow and costly to launch if you touch sensitive or restricted scopes.
time: Prototype: 1 to 2 hours. Sensitive scope verification: days to a few weeks. Restricted scopes (Gmail read, full Drive): weeks to months including a third-party security assessment.

blockers.text: Apps in Testing status are limited to 100 listed test users, and authorizations expire 7 days after consent (including refresh tokens), except apps that only request name, email and profile scopes.
Apps with restricted scopes that access data through a third-party server must pass an annual security assessment by a Google-approved independent assessor (reassessment at least every 12 months).
Needs a verified domain, privacy policy, homepage and a demo video showing scope use.
Unverified apps show a scary warning screen to users.

steps: Create a Cloud project and enable the API (Gmail, Drive, etc).
Configure the OAuth consent screen and add the narrowest scopes possible.
Create an OAuth client ID (web) with redirect URIs.
Prototype in Testing mode with listed test users.
Publish to production and submit for verification; record the demo video.
If restricted scopes: complete the security assessment.
agent: Pick the narrowest scopes and explain why, which directly cuts the review burden
Write the consent-screen justification text and a demo video script
Generate the OAuth flow code and test it with a test user
you: Create the Cloud project and verify domain ownership
Record the demo video and respond to Google reviewers
Pay for and schedule the security assessment if required
uncertain: Assessment pricing and timelines vary by vendor and year.
Verification wait is highly variable per application.
Assessment cost, verified-domain, privacy-policy, demo-video and unverified-app-warning claims were not checked.
Timeline figures (days to weeks, weeks to months) are estimates, not from docs.
